method: Rootless code-path audit with the fake daemon modified to alternate kdebug KdBuf.cpuid values 0 and 4 for successive invented PET/PMC samples. It used the app’s actual submitting thread ID, the real M1 Metal app, Stax server and PR47 capture adapter. No root helper or hardware counters were used.

source_observation.kdebug_input_field: KdBuf.cpuid is a u32 on each raw record
source_observation.parser: stax-mac-kperf-parse/src/parser.rs Sample and State::InSample keep timestamp_ns, tid, stack frames and pmc; they do not retain cpuid
source_observation.aggregator: stax-live/src/aggregator.rs PetSample does not contain cpuid
source_observation.v3_archive: stax-live-proto/src/lib.rs SavedPetSample has timestamp_ns, stack, kernel_stack, pmc; no cpuid
source_observation.topdown_importer: PR47 topdown/stax_archive.py cannot recover a per-sample CPU ID from this v3 archive

limitation: Synthetic CPU ID tags are not measurements of P/E core residency. This control demonstrates that pinned Stax v3 drops the raw CPU ID before archive import. Even a future privileged M1 capture cannot stratify its saved PET/PMC values by core from this archive alone. Preserve core identity upstream, or provide separate independently verified core-scoped captures, before claiming P/E-specific counter interpretation.
